title: FVGs in the Dayli ICC Framework
hook: We don’t force our method to fit another concept.

launchpad.outcome: Keep FVGs as market literacy, never a Dayli ICC requirement.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does a Dayli ICC entry need an FVG?

slides.headline: You are not becoming an FVG trader 😂
slides.line: You’re becoming a trader who understands delivery and keeps her method clean.

slides.title: Two columns.
slides.footer: Look at the right column carefully before the next question.

slides.heading: WHERE IS THE REQUIRED FVG STEP?
slides.body: PIL → Indication → Correction → Continuation → Retest → Entry.

check.prompt: Where in that sequence is the required FVG step?

options.label: There isn’t one
options.why: Exactly. There is no FVG step.

options.label: Between correction and continuation
options.feedback: Read the sequence again. No FVG there.

options.label: Right before entry
options.feedback: The step before entry is the retest. Not an FVG.

slides.title: FVGs are not required for Dayli ICC.
slides.body: A valid Dayli ICC setup does not need:
slides.footer: If FVGs help you understand the chart, great. They never become a requirement.

items.text: Price displaced and left an imbalance. I’ll note it as context.
No FVG, so this valid setup is invalid.
items.why: A valid Dayli ICC setup never needs an FVG.

items.text: I’ll wait for the FVG to fill before I take my entry.
items.why: That adds a rule the method doesn’t have.

items.text: The move was displaced, so participation looked one-sided in that moment.
There’s an FVG, so the entry model is confirmed.
items.why: An FVG never confirms the entry model.

slides.quote: We don’t force our method to fit another concept.

slides.prompt: How do FVGs fit into the way you read a chart, and what don’t they change?
slides.modelAnswer: FVGs help me describe how price delivered and where it moved quickly. They’re context. They don’t change my entry model: Dayli ICC never requires an FVG, a fill, a retest of an FVG, or an FVG entry.

takeaways: There is no FVG step in the Dayli ICC sequence.
No FVG, fill, retest or FVG entry is required.
We don’t force our method to fit another concept.
remember: We don’t force our method to fit another concept.
